title: Selling Plugins Without a Payment Processor: Which Architecture Actually Works for You for Digital Creators
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.

content.text: Digital creators in Nigeria face a stark reality: Stripe, PayPal, and other payment processors block access based on geography, not merit. This isn't a temporary glitch—it's structural exclusion baked into the financial internet. For plugin developers, course creators, and template designers, this means lost revenue, delayed launches, and dependence on unreliable workarounds. Sovereign commerce infrastructure offers a permanent alternative. It replaces rented platforms with owned architecture. This post compares conventional payment processors against self-hosted stacks like the ones COREMERCH deploys. We'll analyze tradeoffs in control, cost, and scalability. The goal is clear: help you choose infrastructure that works under pressure, not just in theory.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Conventional payment processors like Stripe and PayPal offer convenience at the cost of sovereignty. They handle payment processing, fraud detection, and compliance—but only if your country is on their approved list. For digital creators in Nigeria, this convenience is a non-starter. Self-hosted stacks, like COREMERCH's Complete Builder Kit, flip the model. You own the hosting (GitHub Pages/Cloudflare Pages), the backend logic (Cloudflare Workers/Google Apps Script), and the payment verification (NOWPayments). This architecture doesn't ask permission. It uses crypto payments to bypass geographic restrictions. The tradeoff is clear: you exchange ease of setup for infrastructure you control. No platform can shut you down. No algorithm decides your access. This is base-layer ownership, not a workaround.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe and PayPal exclude countries based on regulatory risk, currency instability, or political factors. For Nigerian creators, this means rejection without recourse. Self-hosted stacks sidestep this entirely. By using crypto payments (BTC, USDT, SOL) verified on-chain, they eliminate the need for centralized approval. NOWPayments handles the transaction, firing a webhook the moment payment confirms. This system doesn't care about your location—only about the validity of the transaction. It's infrastructure built for financial isolation, pressure-tested in Zimbabwe during currency collapse. The tradeoff is that you must educate buyers on crypto payments. But once set up, the system operates without geographic bias. It's commerce infrastructure that respects your sovereignty, not your address.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Stripe and PayPal process payments instantly but charge 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. They also hold funds for days or weeks, especially for high-risk accounts. Crypto payments through NOWPayments confirm in minutes (depending on network congestion) with a flat 0.5% fee. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON keep transaction costs under $0.10. Self-hosted stacks add no additional fees. You pay for hosting only if you choose paid tiers (Cloudflare Workers, Supabase). The real cost is time: setting up the stack requires technical knowledge or purchasing a pre-built solution like the Complete Builder Kit. But once deployed, the system operates without recurring fees. It's a one-time investment in infrastructure you own, not a subscription to someone else's platform.
Self-hosted stacks give you infrastructure ownership, not platform rental.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With Stripe and PayPal, you rent access to their systems. They can freeze your account, change their terms, or shut down your integration at any time. Self-hosted stacks give you full ownership. COREMERCH deploys the infrastructure to your accounts—GitHub, Cloudflare, or Google—and hands over the keys. Automation is handled through backend logic (Cloudflare Workers or Apps Script). File delivery uses Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. The system is yours to modify, scale, or relocate. This ownership extends to customer data: orders are stored in Supabase or Google Sheets, under your control. The tradeoff is responsibility. You manage security, updates, and compliance. But in exchange, you gain infrastructure that cannot be taken away.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you're in Nigeria and cannot use Stripe or PayPal, self-hosted stacks are not just an alternative—they're the only permanent solution.
